title: Online, Reachability-Aware, Sampling-Based Motion Planning
text: This work combines the rigorous safety guarantees of reachable-set analysis with the flexibility of sampling-based Model Predictive Control (MPC) planning. By leveraging modern reachability techniques and computation platforms, we compute guaranteed over-approximations of system trajectories under disturbances at runtime, without the need for any expensive pre-computation. These over-approximations allow the planner to choose sampled control signals that are robust to any disturbance realization, rather than considering only nominal state predictions. In a simulated study of a dynamic bicycle model, our technique reduces safety violations by over 99%. On a real, 1/28th scale model racecar, the vehicle successfully completes dozens of laps without any crashes.

title: Online, Reachability-Aware, Sampling-Based Motion Planning
text:
Method Summary
In each control loop, our planner

Samples a large number \(N\) of control signals with finite duration \(T\) around a reference
Integrates an embedding system for each signal, giving interval-valued trajectories guaranteed to contain the state of the original system under any (bounded) disturbance signal
Identifies the set of sampled controls that are provably safe (i.e. whose interval trajectories do not intersect the unsafe set)
Chooses a minimum-cost sampled control from the safe set

By leveraging reachable-set analysis, our controller makes a provable, deterministic safety guarantee about signals in its safe set, avoiding stochastic or incentive-driven approaches to choose safe controls. Furthermore, our interval-based reachability is fast enough to perform all calculations fully online while scaling to high-dimensional state spaces.

title: Experimental Parameter Values
text:
Disturbance bounds: \(\left[\underline{w}_{v_\mathrm{lat}}, \overline{w}_{v_\mathrm{lat}}\right] = [-0.01,\ 0.01]\), \(\left[\underline{w}_{\phi}, \overline{w}_{\phi}\right] = [-0.02,\ 0.02]\)
Control sampling parameters:

Steering parameters: (Difference sampling) \(\Delta u_{\mathrm{std}} = \frac{3}{4}\pi\), \(\left[\underline{\Delta u}_{\mathrm{bnd}}, \overline{\Delta u}_{\mathrm{bnd}}\right] = \left[-\frac{3}{2}\pi,\ \frac{3}{2}\pi\right]\), (Action sampling) \(\left[\underline{u}_{\mathrm{bnd}}, \overline{u}_{\mathrm{bnd}}\right] = [-0.4555,\ 0.4555]\)
Throttle parameters: (Difference sampling) \(\Delta u_{\mathrm{std}} = 1\), \(\left[\underline{\Delta u}_{\mathrm{bnd}}, \overline{\Delta u}_{\mathrm{bnd}}\right] = [-8,\ 2]\), (Action sampling) \(\left[\underline{u}_{\mathrm{bnd}}, \overline{u}_{\mathrm{bnd}}\right] = [-1,\ 1]\)

Kinematic switching speed: \(\hat{v}_{\mathrm{long}} = 0.1\)
Vehicle parameters: \(\ell_f = 0.04824\), \(\ell_r = 0.04176\), \(m = 0.1667\), \(I_z = 0.00045\)

Pacejka slip coefficients: \(B = 2.3\), \(C = 1.6\), \(D = 1.1\)
Motor acceleration model: \(C_a = 6.17\), \(C_v = 15.2\), \(C_e = 0.333\)
